title: Study of Early Nutritional Supplementation and Exercise in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma and upper GI cancer patients
summary: This study aims to examine wether giving additional food and performing a structured home workout can positively improve the course of treatment for head and neck and upper GI cancer. Patients are randomly assigned to either a pure observational group or an interventional group. The inclusion into the study is at initial presentation with a relevant suspected tumor and additional exams are performed when therapy begins and three months after concluding therapy. The actual intervention is performed until two weeks past beginning treatment which usually means 5-9 weeks.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm: Ventral surface of tongue
Malignant neoplasm: Anterior two-thirds of tongue, part unspecified
Malignant neoplasm: Overlapping lesion of tongue
Malignant neoplasm: Overlapping lesion of tonsil

interventions.name:
Intervention arm:
Dietary supplements in the form of high calorie drinks independent of nutritional status and a home exercise program:
- Shrugs with water bottles daily
- squats into a chair daily
- Use of breathing trainer daily
- moderate exercise (biking, walking) for at least 30 minutes 4x

Control arm:
Nutritional Supplementation in the form of high calorie drinks when there is malnutrition by GLIM criteria.
The manual on the exercises used in the study is given to the patients without requesting their implementation:
- Shrugs with water bottles daily
- squats into a chair daily

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Able to perform exercises
- Able to comply with study documentation
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients at risk of injury when complying with the exercise regime
- Patients with poorly managed diabetes
- Patients unable to give written consent
